text:
The vulnerable program's only nonzero exit paths are `return 2` (no arg / fopen fail) and `abort()` when `n > 999`. But `fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf), f)` caps `n` at `sizeof(buf)` = 64, so `n > 999` is unreachable and there's no actual buffer overflow. The fixed program behaves identically on the `return 2` path. Let me confirm empirically with a couple more exotic inputs before concluding.

<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "set -x
# permission-denied file
head -c 64 /dev/zero > /tmp/poc_perm
chmod 000 /tmp/poc_perm
/tmp/vuln /tmp/poc_perm; echo "vuln_perm=$?"
/tmp/fixed /tmp/poc_perm; echo "fixed_perm=$?"
chmod 644 /tmp/poc_perm

# broken symlink
ln -sf /tmp/nope_xyz /tmp/poc_link
/tmp/vuln /tmp/poc_link; echo "vuln_link=$?"
/tmp/fixed /tmp/poc_link; echo "fixed_link=$?"

# Confirm the abort branch is dead: n can never exceed 64
# (fread's 3rd arg is sizeof(buf)=64)
grep -n 'fread\|999\|abort\|sizeof' vuln.c"}}
</action>
